meta.oberthema: Paul Laurence Dunbar, „Sympathy“ – The African American Experience
inhalte: Comment: WSJ zu Obamas Wahl – Rassismus kein Hindernis mehr? (Sklaverei bis heute)
Mediation: E-Mail – Umbenennung der Berliner Mohrenstraße nach Anton Wilhelm Amo

criteria.short: Grundsituation des Gedichts
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling fasst die Grundsituation des Gedichts zusammen, etwa:
bullets: **speaker claims to know** what a caged bird feels
**bird is locked in a cage** and cannot take part in life outside
**speaker's knowledge** seems to come from his own experience
**speaker expresses deep sympathy** with the bird

criteria.short: Gefühle angesichts der Natur draußen (Strophe 1)
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling gibt die Gefühle des Vogels angesichts der Natur draußen wieder (Strophe 1), etwa:
bullets: **beautiful spring day**: the sun shines on the hills
**gentle wind** moves through the fresh grass
**calm, clear river** flows through the landscape
**first birds sing and flowers open** and spread their scent
**bird suffers** because it is shut out from all this

criteria.short: Kampf gegen die Gefangenschaft (Strophe 2)
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling gibt den Kampf des Vogels gegen seine Gefangenschaft wieder (Strophe 2), etwa:
bullets: **bird beats its wings** against the cage
**injures itself** until it bleeds
**has to return to its perch** instead of sitting freely on a branch
**old wounds hurt again**, and the pain grows stronger
**speaker understands** why the bird keeps fighting

criteria.short: Bedeutung des Gesangs (Strophe 3)
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling gibt die Bedeutung des Gesangs wieder (Strophe 3), etwa:
bullets: **bird sings** although it is wounded and in pain
**song does not express joy** or happiness
**song is a prayer** from the depth of its heart
**plea to Heaven** for freedom

criteria.short: These: Zusammenwirken von Bildsprache, Struktur und Stilmitteln
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling entwickelt eine schlüssige These, die aufzeigt, wie Bildsprache, Struktur und Stilmittel zusammenwirken, um das Leiden des Vogels und seine Sehnsucht nach Freiheit zu vermitteln, z. B.:
bullets: **extended metaphor of the caged bird** as image of captivity and suffering, implicitly the oppression of African Americans
**speaker identifies with the bird** ("I know what the caged bird feels", l. 1); title signals shared suffering
**contrast between free nature and the cage** conveys the bird's longing for freedom
**progression across the stanzas** from feeling to physical struggle to prayer intensifies the suffering

criteria.short: Bildsprache und ihre Wirkung
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling analysiert die Bildsprache und ihre Wirkung, z. B.:
bullets: **idyllic spring imagery** of the world outside ("the sun is bright on the upland slopes", l. 2)
**images of awakening life** ("the first bud opes", l. 5) stress a renewal denied to the bird
**violent imagery of self-injury** ("its blood is red on the cruel bars", l. 9)
**perch vs. bough**: confinement against natural freedom ("on the bough a-swing", l. 11)
**"old, old scars"** (l. 12) as image of long-lasting, inherited pain, alluding to slavery
**religious imagery** turns the song into a plea for deliverance ("upward to Heaven he flings", l. 20)

criteria.short: Struktur und ihre Funktion
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling untersucht die Struktur des Gedichts und ihre Funktion, z. B.:
bullets: **three stanzas of seven lines** with parallel build-up; regularity mirrors the confinement of the cage
**refrain framing each stanza** ("I know what the caged bird feels!", l. 7) stresses the speaker's insight
**variation of the refrain** (feels – beats his wing – sings) as climax from emotion to struggle to song
**rhyme scheme ABAAB + final couplet**, mirrored by indentation, creates closure, no way out
**mainly iambic metre with anapaestic variations** gives a song-like rhythm imitating birdsong

criteria.short: Stilmittel und ihre Wirkung
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling untersucht die Stilmittel und ihre Wirkung, z. B.:
bullets: **anaphora "I know"** (ll. 1, 8, 15) underlines the speaker's certainty and identification
**anaphora "When"** (ll. 2, 3, 5) piles up images of freedom and heightens the longing
**interjections** ("alas!", l. 1; "ah me", l. 15) express grief
**personification "cruel bars"** (l. 9) presents the cage as an active oppressor
**antithesis** "not a carol of joy or glee, / But a prayer" (ll. 18–19) reveals the song as desperation

criteria.short: Aussage erläutern und klar Stellung beziehen
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling erläutert die Aussage und bezieht klar Stellung, z. B.:
bullets: **explains the claim**: Obama's victory seen as proof that racism no longer holds African Americans back
**distinguishes legal equality** from equality in everyday life
**takes a clear stand** for or against the statement
**links the claim to the poem's cage**: has it really been opened?

criteria.short: Historische Entwicklung von der Sklaverei bis heute (Unterricht)
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling begründet seine Position mit der historischen Entwicklung von der Sklaverei bis in die Gegenwart unter Rückgriff auf den Unterricht, z. B.:
bullets: **slavery**: centuries of oppression not erased by one election
**Jim Crow laws and segregation** ended only in the 1960s, within living memory
**Rosa Parks and the Civil Rights Movement**: equality won through struggle, still incomplete
**Black history timeline**: Obama as a milestone in a long, slow development
**Obama's election as real progress**: a Black American in the highest office
**racist backlash** during his presidency (e.g. "birther" conspiracy) shows that racism persisted

criteria.short: Dunbars Gedicht in die Argumentation einbeziehen
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling bezieht Dunbars Gedicht in seine Argumentation ein, z. B.:
bullets: **caged bird's suffering** still mirrors the experience of many African Americans
**"old, old scars"** (l. 12): the legacy of slavery is still felt today
**one bird outside the cage** does not free the others: Obama as an exception
**the bird's plea** (l. 20) parallels present-day calls for justice (e.g. Black Lives Matter)
**a poem from 1899 still relevant**, which shows how long the struggle has lasted

criteria.short: Begründetes Urteil
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling gelangt zu einem begründeten Urteil, z. B.:
bullets: **rejects the claim**: symbolic progress, but structural racism persists
**agrees (partly)** if convincingly argued (e.g. legal equality, Black leaders in politics)
**outlook**: what still has to change for the cage to open

Erläutert, wer Anton Wilhelm Amo war
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling erläutert, wer Anton Wilhelm Amo war, etwa:
bullets: born in **present-day Ghana**, **enslaved as a child** (1707) by the Dutch East India Company
**given as a "present"** to the ducal court of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel
nevertheless received an **exceptional education**
**first known Black scholar** at a German university, Enlightenment philosopher with a **doctorate from Wittenberg** (1734)
wrote a disputation on the **rights of Black people in Europe**
left Germany in 1747 after a **racist smear campaign**, returned to his home country, where his traces are lost

criteria.short: Erläutert, warum die Straße umbenannt wurde
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling erläutert, warum die Straße umbenannt wurde, etwa:
bullets: the street had carried its name **since 1706**, for more than 300 years
district: the name has a **"racist core"** (old colonial term for Black people, comparable to the N-word)
it **damages Berlin's reputation**
Germany's colonial past was **long ignored or played down**
there is a growing need to **confront racist structures**
**renaming tainted street names** is a central demand in this debate
the decision followed a **long debate** and **pressure from civil society** initiatives
Berlin's public transport company (BVG) had already planned to **rename the underground station**
the new name will **commemorate the presence of Black people** in Germany

criteria.short: Skizziert die Reaktionen auf die Entscheidung
criteria.intro: Der Prüfling skizziert die Reaktionen auf die Entscheidung, etwa:
bullets: **AfD** (far-right party): the city's **cultural identity is endangered**
the **CDU** (conservatives) also **opposed** the renaming
the decision was based on a **motion by the Greens and SPD**
**Black community and anti-colonial initiatives** (ISD, Decolonize) **campaigned for Amo**
**Humboldt University institute** at the end of the street and a neighbourhood initiative **supported the renaming**
Prof. Römhild: using the address was **unbearable**, as her discipline is itself **entangled in colonial history**
author: streets linked to the **Nazi era or the GDR were renamed without problems**
author: holding on to colonial names reflects **everyday racism**

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling richtet seinen Text konsequent und explizit auf die Intention und den Adressatenkreis im Sinne der Aufgabenstellung aus, berücksichtigt den situativen Kontext, beachtet die Textsortenmerkmale des geforderten Zieltextformats, erstellt einen sachgerecht strukturierten Text und gestaltet seinen Text hinreichend ausführlich, aber ohne unnötige Wiederholungen und Umständlichkeiten.
